hrmq-dashboard-steering-indicators replaces the prior 15-widget queue-depth Dashboard (12 stat tiles + 3 object-table lists) with 6 steering indicators. Billable ratio and Headcount & turnover bind via dataSource (raw GraphQL, no new backend endpoint, unguarded — the same exposure every Employees/Timesheets index page already has today); the filter/tenant-scoping token grammar (`@workspace.activeAdministrationId?`) does NOT apply to the raw-GraphQL dataSource form (`useDataSource.js`'s `queryAndVars` passes `graphql.query`/`graphql.variables` through unresolved — confirmed by reading the composable, both in the sibling source tree and the installed dist), so these two widgets are UNSCOPED across administrations rather than carrying the (broken, per brief §6) sentinel token — no worse than today's index-page exposure, but not literally what design.md D4 describes either. Both are also single-series, not the two-named-series design.md's D1 table describes: `useDataSource`'s raw-GraphQL `selectors` map performs one dot-path pluck per output key (`selectByPath` in `useGraphQL.js`) with no mechanism to assemble two differently-aliased root fields into one `[{name,data}]` series array — verified against the installed dist, not just the source tree. Absence rate / Payroll cost per period / Approval lead time bind via `endpointSource` to the new guarded `AnalyticsController::trends()` (REQ-DSI-004/006/007); Obligations binds via `endpointSource` to `AnalyticsController::obligations()` (REQ-DSI-008/009). All three trend `endpointSource` widgets go through the local `chart` widgetKey override (`registry.js` → `src/widgets/TrendChartWidget.vue`), which does its OWN null-safe series mapping rather than delegating to CnChartWidget's native `endpointSource` prop — that prop's own `Number(value) || 0` mapping (`CnChartWidget.vue`'s `endpointChartData`, confirmed in the installed dist) silently turns a `null` bucket into `0`, which is exactly the 'measurement that never ran reads as a good result' failure REQ-DSI-004's null-not-zero contract exists to prevent. The `chart` widgetKey is ALSO overridden for a second, independent reason: CnChartWidget (registered in the library's dashboard-widget catalog) was built to be embedded inside CnDashboardPage's own per-widget template, which supplies the title bar externally — it has no `title` prop and does not self-wrap in CnWidgetWrapper, and `CnWidgetGrid` (the only renderer hrmq's pages use, since every page has a `slot:"body"` widget) mounts it bare. `TrendChartWidget.vue` bridges both gaps — the SAME `effectiveRegistry`-wins-over-catalog mechanism `registry.js` already uses for `stat`, and the same bridge-a-mismatched-library-component pattern already used for `actions`/`lifecycle-actions`. The Obligations `object-table` widget uses CnWidgetObjectTable's REAL flat prop names directly (`endpointSource`/`columns`/`emptyText`, siblings of `title` under `props`) rather than nesting them under a `content` key the way the removed 'Aflopende contracten'/'Aflopende BHV-certificaten' widgets did — CnWidgetObjectTable declares no `content` prop (confirmed in both the source tree and the installed dist), so that nested shape would not have reached the component; a per-row route to each obligation's own detail page (SickLeaveCaseDetail/EmploymentContractDetail/BhvCertificeringDetail, varying by row TYPE) is not wired: CnWidgetObjectTable's `rowRoute` is a single STATIC route-name string for the whole table, not a per-row dynamic selector, so the endpoint's own per-row `route` field is carried in the response but not yet clickable from this widget.

config._note: single-person-modes (REQ-SPM-006/D5): a self-service surface for the EXISTING nl-gebruikelijkloon-norm verdict for the caller's own DGA Employee. The whole menu entry is visibleIf-gated on administrationMode: dga_single_person (D2/D3). The warning banner is bound to the read-only, stateless GET /apps/hrmq/api/payroll/dga-status endpoint (PayrollController::dgaStatus, which REUSES NlDgaChecks' predicate -- zero new tax logic, zero new persistence): visibleWhen {endpoint, field: met, op: eq, value: false} renders it only when the caller's own annualised loon is below norm AND unjustified. The endpoint takes no per-object parameter (it always means 'my own record', D5.1), so the visibleWhen.endpoint non-templated same-origin path applies cleanly -- no object id to interpolate, the documented fallback (a custom widget) is not needed. Fail-safe: the banner stays hidden on a 404 (no Employee, or Employee not a DGA -- both collapse to the same status, D5.1) or any fetch failure, so a non-DGA caller who somehow reaches this route sees no alert. The info banner is always visible and explains the page. Both widgets are built-in `banner` (CnBannerWidget) -- no custom component, no single-widget-dashboard anti-pattern.

config._note: Hub archetype: Employee is the record every other HR/payroll schema in hrmq points AT (EmploymentContract.employeeId, Payslip.employeeId, Timesheet.employeeId, Expense.employeeId — all now canonical $ref relations, ADR-062 rule 7), so the page's job is to be the single place an HR/payroll admin lands to see one person's whole labour and pay picture. ADR-062 round-2 rework: the data widget is SPLIT into 'Person' (employeeNumber/firstName/lastName/dateOfBirth/bsn — the identity attributes) at 8-wide beside an in-grid stats-block (KPIs, top-right — replaces the deprecated summaryAggregates header chips) at 4-wide; 'Employment & compliance' (startDate/endDate/grossMonthlySalary/taxTableColor/ID-document retention/30%-ruling incl. start/end date + reduced-norm flag (30-procent-regeling)/A1 posting/jurisdiction-specific onboarding flags — 21 fields, genuinely this schema's bulk) runs full-width below since it has no natural width-4 partner. Contracts and Timesheets are paired FK-scoped lists, then Payslips (allowCreate:false — payroll-generated, not hand-created from here) and Expenses, then org-chart-basic (2026-07-13) adds an Assignments FK-scoped list (OrgAssignment.employeeId — the placements this employee holds across the org hierarchy) as a full-width row, and performance-reviews-mvp (2026-07-13) adds a Beoordelingen FK-scoped list (PerformanceReview.employeeId — the ADR-001 Rule 6 dossier anchoring: performance data lives on the personnel dossier, not a separate module) as a further full-width row, and goals-okr (2026-07-15) adds a Doelen & OKR's FK-scoped list (Objective.employeeId — the measurable, cross-review sibling of Beoordelingen; team objectives live on OrgUnit and do not appear here) as a further full-width row, and comp-cycles (2026-07-15) adds a Beloningsvoorstellen FK-scoped list (CompAdjustment.employeeId — the ADR-001 Rule 6 'Functie & comp' detail-surface anchoring: compensation-review proposals live on the personnel dossier, not a separate module) as a further full-width row, and leave-buy-sell (2026-07-15) adds a Verlof kopen/verkopen FK-scoped list (LeaveTransaction.employeeId, rowRoute LeaveTransactionDetail) as a further full-width row, before the personnel-file Files leaf, which shifts down again. NO calendar/contacts/talk: Employee declares no appointment or comms linkedType — the person's own identity data lives on this record, it is not a link to a separate NC contact. No lifecycleActions — Employee carries no x-openregister-lifecycle. Audit history stays a sidebar tab.

hrmq-personal-dashboard (design.md D1/D3): the caller-scoped personal landing surface hydra ADR-097 Decision 3 requires — 'route to a type: "dashboard" page scoped to the caller … Not an index page, and not a bare parent with no route of its own'. The MijnHrGroup menu entry gains route: "MijnHr" through this fragment's menu block (mergeMenuItems fills the base group's undefined route key), so the group title lands here while its nine children stay under the collapse chevron — both of Decision 3's conditions, which moves hrmq's counted main-menu total from 6 to 5. Every widget carries a caller-scope filter (userId: "@me", or managerUserId: "@me" for the approver's own queue) plus the OPTIONAL administration token @workspace.activeAdministrationId? — unresolved means dropped, so a widget degrades to user-scoped-only, never to another user's rows. Only the built-in `stat` and `object-table` types are used (stat resolves through hrmq's own registry.js override, which is load-bearing: the library's self-registration is tree-shaken out of the production bundle); no custom widget, no new backend endpoint, no raw-GraphQL dataSource (the steering Dashboard's _note documents why that form resolves a schema by name across every register on the instance). Widget 6 has no conditional-visibility primitive available — the dashboard widget grammar has none for stat tiles (design.md D4) — so it always renders and shows 0 for a caller who manages nobody; its caption keeps the zero legible. The stat tiles' click-through uses content.route in the vue-router LOCATION-OBJECT form ({"name": "…"}), not the bare string design.md D3 writes: widgetLink passes a string straight to <router-link :to>, where vue-router 4 reads it as a PATH, so a bare route NAME would fall through to the catch-all. Same spelling the hr-objects nav-card entries already use. The three object-table widgets carry the FLAT content contract (register/schema/filter/sort{field,dir}/limit/columns/rowRoute/viewAllRoute/emptyText), NOT the nested `source` shape design.md D3 writes — measured live 2026-08-22, not inferred: on a type:"dashboard" page CnDashboardPage.registryRenderer looks up getWidgetTypeEntry(canonicalWidgetType(type)), and utils/widgetTypeAliases.js maps `object-table` -> `table`, which registerDashboardWidgets.js registers INLINE to CnObjectListWidget. The alias therefore never reaches CnWidgetObjectTable's dashboardRegistration (its `object-table` key is registered under a name the canonicaliser has already rewritten away, in a side-effect module ADR-061 tree-shaking drops anyway). With the `source` shape the widget rendered its emptyText and fired ZERO fetches, because CnObjectListWidget reads content.register/content.schema and has no `source` key at all. Consequences of the real contract, accepted: `limit` is a FETCH CAP (ADR-062), not a render promise — the visible row count fits the cell — and there is no per-row-route escape, which is fine since rowRoute is already a single static route name. All three also carry allowCreate: false — CnObjectListWidget renders a "+ Toevoegen" create affordance by DEFAULT (measured live), and all three collections are read-only to the employee: Timesheets are server-created by the booking flow (MijnUrenstaten already sets showAdd: false), LeaveBalance is written only by LeaveAccrualJob, and payslips are payroll-generated (REQ-MHS-004's read-only posture). Labels are Dutch literals; hrmq-i18n-locale-completeness owns their conversion and this change adds no English keys.
